description: The container/codec/duration checks and the must-sound floor can all fail, on the same four artifacts the entry's historical run_ids name: two voiced chalk muxes pass with must-sound on, a silent-by-design mux passes report-only and trips the floor when the same bytes are ASSERTED to sound, an audio-free dispatch mux passes when absence is declared and produces an honest FAIL when sound is claimed, and a true file placed outside its authoring envelope is caught by duration alone.
notes: rcos-eval/2: this package declares NO adapter of its own. It names the registered
capability and the input document, and the run reaches the capability through the
invocation kernel — `rcos run audio-offline-verify --input ...` takes the identical
path. The thing being evaluated is the thing reuse will call.
This replaces NOTHING. The two eval entries already on the registry entry
('chalk-vo-and-silent-mux' and the chalk1+dispatch one) are historical assertions and
stay byte-for-byte as written; this receipt is a new record that links backward by
exercising the SAME checker (capabilities/audio-offline-verify/adapter/av_check.py,
sha256 29eb2d8f…, pinned in gates/check.js) on the SAME four fixture files the
historical logs name, whose sha256 are pinned in the artifact_identity_pinned gate.
Every probe reproduces a line from a committed historical log rather than inventing
an expectation: evidence/audio-offline-verify/{eval-1,eval-2,eval-3-chalk1,eval-3-dispatch}.log
and attack/{mute-caught,no-audio-stream}.log. Two probes are authored controls with no
historical counterpart (chalk2_wrong_envelope, dispatch_absent_expect_none): the first
proves the duration gate bites on bytes that otherwise pass, the second exercises the
`--expect-audio none` branch that EVAL.json declares but the historical log never ran.
The RMS pins carry a 0.5 dB tolerance. The historical values (-35.113250 and
-35.104884 dBFS) are what astats reported on this box's ffmpeg; a different ffmpeg
build may report a slightly different RMS for the same bytes. Container facts
(duration, codec, dimensions, sample rate, channel count) are exact pins — they are
metadata, not measurements.
Recorded as-is, not corrected: the capability README's contract paragraph names the
flags `--min-s, --max-s` while the frozen checker implements `--min-duration,
--max-duration`. The eval passes the flags the SCRIPT accepts; the documentation
mismatch is a fact about the artifact, not something this package rewrites.
